Boston 8 - Decision Tree (Regression) with Bagging, Raondom Forest and Boosting with 5-fold Cross Validation

Nao Mimoto - Dept. of Statistics : The University of Akron – Class Web Page

  • 1. Load Data and Prepare
  • 2. Data Separation
  • 3. Decision Tree has high variance (CV.train fit only)
  • 4. Decision Tree Growing using rpart(). It has color plotting.
  • 5. Decision Tree (Grow and Prune using tree())
  • 6. Bagging (Train and Test only)
  • 7. Radnom Forest (Train and Test)
  • 8. Boosting (Train and Test)
  • 9. OLS for comparison
  • CODE ONLY

1. Load Data and Prepare

(top)

library(tidyverse)           # install.packages("tidyverse")
Boston <- as_tibble(Boston)

2. Data Separation

(top)

# Load the file from my website
source("https://nmimoto.github.io/R/ML-00.txt")   # load CreateCV()


# Use this function to create CV dataset
my.seed=3231
CreateCV(Orig, numFolds=5, seed=my.seed)
## 
##     number of folds:  5 
##     number of obs:  506 
##     training data:  84  x  5  =  420 
##     size of test data:  86 
## 
##     Global variables created:  
##       Train.set       Train.resp           
##       Test.set        Test.resp            
##       CV.train[[k]]   CV.train.resp[[k]]   
##       CV.valid[[k]]   CV.valid.resp[[k]]
# Output (all as Data Frame):
#   Train.set      Train.resp
#   Test.set       Test.resp
#   CV.train[[[[k]]]]  CV.train.resp[[[[k]]]]
#   CV.valid[[[[k]]]]  CV.valid.resp[[[[k]]]]


#--- plot Training and Test for visualization
fold = 2
plot(CV.train[[fold]]$lstat,  CV.train[[fold]]$resp, xlab="lstat", ylab="Response (medv)")
lines(CV.valid[[fold]]$lstat, CV.valid[[fold]]$resp, type="p", col="red", pch=19)


3. Decision Tree has high variance (CV.train fit only)

(top)

library(tree)          # install.packages('tree', repos='https://cran.case.edu/')
tree31 <- tree(resp ~., CV.train[[1]])
summary(tree31)
## 
## Regression tree:
## tree(formula = resp ~ ., data = CV.train[[1]])
## Variables actually used in tree construction:
## [1] "lstat"   "rm"      "tax"     "ptratio" "nox"     "crim"   
## Number of terminal nodes:  11 
## Residual mean deviance:  13.93 = 4527 / 325 
## Distribution of residuals:
##     Min.  1st Qu.   Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max. 
## -14.5800  -2.0430  -0.2444   0.0000   1.9540  29.2500
plot(tree31)
text(tree31, pretty=1, cex=.7)

#---------
tree32 <- tree(resp ~., CV.train[[2]])
summary(tree32)
## 
## Regression tree:
## tree(formula = resp ~ ., data = CV.train[[2]])
## Variables actually used in tree construction:
## [1] "lstat" "rm"    "rad"   "nox"  
## Number of terminal nodes:  8 
## Residual mean deviance:  16.3 = 5348 / 328 
## Distribution of residuals:
##      Min.   1st Qu.    Median      Mean   3rd Qu.      Max.

plot(tree32)
text(tree32, pretty=0, cex=.7)


4. Decision Tree Growing using rpart(). It has color plotting.

tree00<- rpart(resp~., data=Train.set)

5. Decision Tree (Grow and Prune using tree())

(top)

#--- a. Growing the tree
library(tree)     # install.packages('tree', repos='https://cran.case.edu/')
tree1 = tree(resp~., Train.set)
summary(tree1)
## 
## Regression tree:
## tree(formula = resp ~ ., data = Train.set)
## Variables actually used in tree construction:
## [1] "rm"      "lstat"   "dis"     "crim"    "ptratio"
## Number of terminal nodes:  9 
## Residual mean deviance:  13.58 = 5580 / 411 
## Distribution of residuals:
##     Min.  1st Qu.   Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max. 
## -17.6800  -2.2180   0.1701   0.0000   2.2820  17.6800
tree1
## node), split, n, deviance, yval
##       * denotes terminal node
## 
##  1) root 420 36320.0 22.55  
##    2) rm < 6.797 341 13620.0 19.59  
##      4) lstat < 14.4 201  5462.0 22.99  
##        8) dis < 1.38485 5   390.7 45.58 *
##        9) dis > 1.38485 196  2454.0 22.41  
##         18) rm < 6.543 165  1493.0 21.62 *
##         19) rm > 6.543 31   304.3 26.64 *
##      5) lstat > 14.4 140  2496.0 14.71  
##       10) crim < 6.91188 80   790.1 17.01 *
##       11) crim > 6.91188 60   718.9 11.64 *
##    3) rm > 6.797 79  6780.0 35.34  
##      6) rm < 7.445 54  2371.0 30.89  
##       12) crim < 7.39342 49  1134.0 32.32 *
##       13) crim > 7.39342 5   166.9 16.96 *
##      7) rm > 7.445 25  1031.0 44.96  
##       14) ptratio < 17.9 20   269.2 47.08 *
##       15) ptratio > 17.9 5   312.7 36.48 *
plot(tree1)
text(tree1, pretty=0, cex=1)

# Check the training fit and test prediction
Train.fitted = predict(tree1, type="vector")
Test.pred    = predict(tree1, Test.set, type="vector")

# Training fit and Test pred plot
plot(Train.fitted, as.matrix(Train.resp), xlab="Fitted", ylab="Actual")
lines(Test.pred, as.matrix(Test.resp), type="p", col="red", pch=19)
abline(0,1, col="red")

GrowOnly <- data.frame(
    tr.RMSE      = caret::RMSE(Train.fitted, as.matrix(Train.resp)),
    tr.Rsquare   = caret::R2(Train.fitted, Train.resp),
    test.RMSE    = caret::RMSE(Test.pred, as.matrix(Test.resp)),
    test.Rsquare = caret::R2(Test.pred, Test.resp)
)
GrowOnly

#1 4.946511 0.6353647


#----------------------
#--- b. Pruning the tree
set.seed(my.seed)
cv.for.pruning = cv.tree(tree1, FUN=prune.tree, K=5)   #5-fold CV
     #use FUN= prune.misclass if you are doing classification tree
names(cv.for.pruning)
## [1] "size"   "dev"    "k"      "method"
plot(cv.for.pruning$size, cv.for.pruning$dev, type="b")

plot(cv.for.pruning$k,    cv.for.pruning$dev, type="b")

                                        # size is the number of terminal nodes
                                        # dev is the Av. CV error rate
                                        # k is the pruning parameter (alpha)
cv.for.pruning

# In this case, it's probably better not to purne.  If you want to prune, use below.

text(pruned2, pretty=0, cex=1)

# For pruned tree, check the training fit and test prediction
